name: Aldous Pryke
summary: Moneylender and churchwarden. Founder of the Pryke Almshouse for the destitute of Harrowgate. Described in his obituary, which he drafted, as "a friend to the poor".

entries.text: Endowed the Pryke Almshouse "from his own purse".
Foreclosed on forty households in the mill closure of 1879 ("lawful recovery").
Sharp practice in the drafting of loan terms.

hidden.text: Falsified his ledgers to double the debts of those he then foreclosed.

archive.title: Almshouse deed, 1881
cards: Deed of gift: the Pryke Almshouse, raised on Plots 1-40, Mill Lane, Harrowgate.
Schedule: said plots 'recovered by A. Pryke from defaulting tenants, 1879'.
Rule 4: each inmate to pay 2d. weekly 'towards the founder's outlay'.

archive.title: Pryke's private ledger
cards: Two ledgers, one hand. The bank's copy dates the loans 1877. His own: 1875.
Interest run from the earlier dates doubles every debt on the Mill Lane book.
Last page, in pencil: 'Forty accounts closed. Plots clear for the almshouse.'

fact.text: The almshouse stands on the forty foreclosed plots and charged its inmates rent.
Two sets of books: he doubled the debts of the households he foreclosed.

answer: I did. Every brick. I have the receipts. I always have the receipts.
questions.card: Says he paid for every brick, and has the receipts.

answer: A modest contribution teaches thrift. You will find it was all perfectly legal.
questions.card: Calls the inmates' rent 'a modest contribution'. Insists it was legal.

answer: ...A man keeps a working copy. I should like to speak to whoever is senior to you.
questions.card: Calls the second ledger 'a working copy'. Asks for your superior.

heaven: A week later the Bright Ministries query the admission, politely, in triplicate.
Your Order rating takes the dent.
hell: The Wardens open an account in his name. He asks for the terms in writing and is given them. All of them.

ext.mitigating: Raised in a debtors' prison himself; he knew exactly what he was doing to them.
